images.title: Square cuts corner equally
images.purpose: Show that a diagonal cuts a corner into two equal angles only when the two sides at the corner are equal, that is a square.
images.composition: Two shapes side by side with wide space: a longer rectangle on the left and a square on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm with one diagonal in grey #6B7280 and the two angles at the bottom left corner shaded teal #0072B2 (about 34 degrees) and amber #E69F00 (about 56 degrees). Right: one square with sides of 5 cm and one diagonal in grey, the two angles at the bottom left corner shaded teal #0072B2 and amber #E69F00, equal in size, each exactly 45 degrees. Exactly 2 shapes, 2 diagonals.

images.takeaway: Equal angles at the corner happen only for a square.
images.description: Left a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle with its diagonal giving about 34 and 56 degrees; right a 5 cm square with its diagonal giving 45 and 45 degrees.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to compare the two angle pairs and say which shape gives equal angles.

image_decisions.why: The contrast between the two shapes carries the idea.
